answers.core:
Yes. The Inspector rendering of exported properties is implemented in the Godot editor itself and cannot be meaningfully altered from an add-on without fully replacing or duplicating Inspector behavior.

This proposal concerns a core limitation of how flags enums are displayed in the Inspector and would benefit all C# users (and potentially other languages) who rely on flags enums with a zero value. An opt-in core solution avoids fragmented, project-specific hacks and provides a consistent, engine-level improvement to editor UX.
answers.workaround:
It can technically be worked around by duplicating enums specifically for Inspector usage and manually mapping them to the runtime enums. However, this is not a simple or clean workaround: it introduces duplicated types, extra maintenance cost, and potential for desynchronization between editor-facing and runtime APIs.

This workaround becomes increasingly problematic in larger frameworks or plugins with many flags enums.

title: Add optional way to hide zero/"None" entry for exported flags enums in Inspector
